title: CLAUDE.md
text: Two core S4 classes flow pipeline: metaXpressStudy — output Module 1, input Modules 2–3. Extends SummarizedExperiment: - assay(study, "counts"): raw count matrix (genes × samples) - colData(study): sample metadata (must contain condition); study$condition works - rowData(study): optional gene annotation (e.g. gene_length TPM) - extra slots: accession, organism, qc_score, de_result - Build metaXpressStudy(); convert SE/DESeqDataSet mx_from_se() (se, "metaXpressStudy") - Never use study@metadata — SE free-form list, sample data. Internally use .counts(), .samples(), .set_counts() (R/utils.R) metaXpressResult — output Module 4, input Modules 5–8: - meta_table: gene-level results (meta-p, meta-FDR, meta-effect size, ²) - method, n_studies, heterogeneity, pathway_result

title: metaXpress: End-to-End Bulk RNA-seq Meta-Analysis
text: Combining bulk RNA-seq studies usually patchwork: one package download GEO data, ad-hoc scripts QC gene ID mapping, separate DE run per study, another package meta-statistics, yet another pathways plots. hand-chance silently drop genes, mix identifiers, lose track study failed QC. metaXpress replaces patchwork one reproducible pipeline built two S4 objects pass cleanly step step. One workflow, end end. GEO ingestion → QC → harmonization → per-study DE → meta-analysis → pathways → figures → report, mx_* functions chain directly. Study quality explicit. 10-point QC checklist (derived Heberle et al., 2025) scores every study, weak cohorts filtered documented criteria rather intuition. Statistically sound design. DE always run independently per study (DESeq2, edgeR limma-voom) combining — never pooled — avoiding batch-confounded inference. Choose right meta-method. Six methods (Fisher, Stouffer, inverse-normal, fixed effects, DerSimonian–Laird random effects, AWmeta) behind single method argument, ² heterogeneity reported every gene. Missing genes handled, hidden. Genes absent studies reported either imputed filtered coverage, instead disappearing intersect. Biology, just gene lists. Cross-study ORA/GSEA, transcription factor activity, cell-composition meta-analysis, consensus co-expression modules drug-reversal ranking turn meta-signatures testable hypotheses. Publication-ready reproducible. Volcano, forest, heatmap, UpSet heterogeneity plots, plus HTML/PDF reports CSV/Excel export captured session info. Scales BiocParallel. Per-study steps parallelize box laptops clusters.

title: Score a study against the 10-point QC checklist — mx_qc_study
text: 10 criteria : Minimum sample size: least 3 samples per condition     group, required reliable dispersion estimation negative binomial     models (Schurch et al. 2016). Sequencing depth: median library size >= 10 million reads,     ensuring adequate power detecting low-abundance transcripts     (Sims et al. 2014). Alignment rate: mean alignment rate >= 70%, indicating     acceptable read quality (optional; skipped available). rRNA contamination: mean rRNA fraction < 10%, flagging     insufficient ribosomal depletion (optional). Duplicate rate: mean duplicate rate < 50%, flagging     library complexity issues (optional). Gene detection: least 15,000 genes detected >= 50%     samples, confirming adequate transcriptome coverage. Metadata completeness: required columns condition     sample_id present. Clear case/control: exactly two condition levels, ensuring     well-defined contrast differential expression. batch-condition confounding: batch condition     perfectly aliased, make batch correction impossible     (Leek et al. 2010). Raw counts: data non-negative integers maximum     > 1,000, confirming untransformed count data suitable count-based     statistical models.

title: metaXpress 0.99.0
text: Initial Bioconductor submission. Module 1: Data ingestion GEO/SRA local files 10-point QC scoring. Module 2: Normalization (TMM, VST, CPM, TPM, quantile) batch correction (ComBat-seq, ComBat, limma, harmony). Module 3: Per-study differential expression via DESeq2, edgeR, limma-voom. Module 4: Meta-analysis statistics — Fisher, Stouffer, inverse-normal, fixed effects, random effects (DerSimonian-Laird), AWmeta. Module 5: Missing gene handling imputation coverage filtering. Module 6: Pathway meta-analysis using KEGG, Reactome, GO, MSigDB Hallmarks. Module 7: Publication-ready visualization (volcano, forest, heatmap, UpSet plots). Module 8: Reproducible HTML/PDF report generation result export.
